h1: Apartment interior design in Warsaw, custom furniture and turnkey renovation, 43 m²

blocks.text: Apartment interior design in Warsaw, custom furniture and turnkey renovation, 43 m²

parts.html: A 43 m² apartment in Warsaw, completed. The studio produced the interior design project and technical documentation, and the studio’s local partners used them to carry out a turnkey renovation and make the custom furniture. The last stage was sewing the curtains and decorating.

The interior is contemporary and leans toward minimalism: beige walls, light oak-effect flooring, fronts with no unnecessary decoration and a few accents in dark wood and brass. With only 43 m², storage had to be built in wherever possible, so almost all the furniture was made to fit the walls.

blocks.text: Living room, kitchen and dining table

parts.html: The living room, kitchen and dining area are one space. The TV wall is made of beige panels with a strip of vertical slats in the center and a long, low oak-effect unit below. To its right are two tall cabinets, with an open niche between them fitted with shelves and LED lighting along the edge.

The kitchen is L-shaped and fits into a small alcove. The upper cabinets are white and go up to the ceiling, the base cabinets are light beige, and all fronts are handleless. The backsplash is laid with large concrete-effect tiles, the sink and faucet are black, the oven is built in under the cooktop, and next to it is a tall pantry cabinet. On the dining side, a tall column cabinet with a wood-effect front separates the kitchen. The studio designs compact kitchens like this for apartments in Bratislava and Vienna too; see the custom kitchens page for more.

The dining area sits between the kitchen and living room: a round dark wood table on a fluted base, chairs in light bouclé and a brass chandelier with exposed bulbs. The cabinet by the entrance is finished with the same beige paneling, with vertical slots cut into the upper part.

The bedroom has a floor-to-ceiling wardrobe across the whole wall. The fronts are fluted and light beige, with short brass handles. The bed has an upholstered base in light fabric, and above it hangs a chandelier with fabric shades on a brass frame.

The entrance hall floor is laid with large gray tiles. Opposite the front door is a tall arched mirror framed with slats in the same beige. The gallery below shows photos of the finished apartment and the furniture made for it, as well as the project visualizations.
